newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES BARELY LOWER IN THIN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES BARELY LOWER IN THIN TRADE.

text.p: Istanbul shares edged lower in continued weak trade on Monday as liquidity shortage persisted due to a forthcoming holiday as well as political caution, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed three points, or 0.2 percent lower at 1,502 after drifting in a narrow range between 1,493 and 1,515. It had lost 4.1 percent last week. Trade volume dropped to 13.13 trillion lira from Friday's 14.13 trillion.

A 4-1/2-day religious holiday between April 17-21 will be followed by an official holiday on April 23. The Exchange said the stock market would close from mid-Thursday until April 24 after the government declared April 22 a holiday for public offices.
"Political uncertainty and the National Security Council (MGK) meeting due on April 26 hinders demand," Murat Elbelger from Finans investment said.
Investors switching to cash or repo deals ahead of the holiday caused volume to shrink last week.
Several brokers await some buying in the next two days when settlements of transactions will be delayed to after the holiday.
"The index may continue to drift between 1,480 support and 1,530 resistance in the short term. More trade volume is needed for it to exceed this range," Elbelger said.

Of the 244 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 104 to 68 and 72 closed stable. The IMKB Industrial eased 0.2 percent to 1,497, the IMKB Services edged down 0.07 percent to 1,413 and the IMKB Financial went down 0.19 percent to 1,610.

Leading actives were state petroleum products marketer Petrol Ofisi's rights issues, steady at 31,500 lira and old shares, down 500 lira at 37,500 and readywear exporter EGS Dis Ticaret, up 1,250 lira at 25,750. They made up 16.2 percent of the total turnover.

Petrol Ofisi issued 1.3777 rights and 0.4 bonus for one existing share on March 31 to increase its capital and coupons used to collect the preemptive rights can trade separately on a special market until May 23, the Exchange said.
